description:
Surfaced 2026-05-12 by project-tier POLYBIUS via HUMAN_relay_substrate_bw_scaling_findings_2026-05-12.md (in ariadne-core-workspace). Substantive substrate-routing knowledge captured during the bw → Ariadne integration arc.

## Background

The ariadne--8fd integration arcs Phase 4 bulk-seed operator action hit an empirical bw scaling wall (O(N) or worse per write at scale; ~50-80h projected for 11,446-ticket corpus). Root cause confirmed via STRABO source-read against jallum/beadwork main: TreeFS.Commit rewrites the entire tree on every commit rather than using incremental tree updates. Comparative research showed every mature git-as-database project (git-bug, public-inbox, Steve Yegges beads-on-Dolt) has built a sidecar projection layer; bw does not.

The project pivoted (factory-manager investigative-workflow demo, ~300-500 tickets, bws sweet spot) rather than forking bw to add a projection layer. The architectural insight is substrate-tier-worth: this matrix should be substrate canon so future POLYBIUS sessions reaching for bw consult it before committing to a use case bw cannot handle.

## Two substrate-canon items

### 1. The bw-fit matrix

Lands in operating-disciplines.md as a section on tool-selection / substrate-choice. Verbatim from the project-tier relay:

| Use case shape | Fit |
|---|---|
| Project-management substrate, incremental over months/years, < ~5k lifetime tickets | bw is the right choice |
| Agent-team work-tracking with rich metadata + dependencies | bw is the right choice (Stoas own use) |
| Investigative workflow with structured evidence + hypotheses | bw is the right choice |
| Audit trail for a workflow with versioned commits | bw is the right choice |
| Catalog / reference corpus / knowledge-graph at 10k+ entries | NOT bw — use direct Postgres, beads-on-Dolt, or another DB engine |
| High-write-rate bulk ingest workloads | NOT bw — even if total corpus is small |
| Use cases requiring concurrent multi-agent cell-level merge | NOT bw (consider beads-on-Dolt if this is a real requirement) |

### 2. The layered-architecture framing

Lands in operating-disciplines.md alongside the matrix (or in a new section on Stoa-canonical-stack):

**bw is the write-side substrate; Ariadne is the read-side projection; hypergraph extends the projection to relational reads.** Each layer addresses a different read shape. Dont force bw to be fast at reads — that is not its job in the stack.

This is a substantive mental model for any future Stoa-deployed project that needs both ticket-shape and knowledge-shape data. It captures the lesson the bw → Ariadne integration arc was actually proving — bw alone wont carry the knowledge-graph use case; the projection layer is load-bearing.

## Gauntlet

ADA + CATO eyeball. Substrate doc-only edit; no code change. ~30-50 LOC of substrate prose.

## Sequencing

P2. Substrate hygiene worth landing before the next project picks bw for the wrong use case. Ride with next substrate-grooming dispatch alongside stoa--148, stoa--nax, dyb, bxx, v2o.

## Empirical anchor

Project-tier relay at HUMAN_relay_substrate_bw_scaling_findings_2026-05-12.md in ariadne-core-workspace; research artifacts in agents/research/bw-scaling-vs-mature-systems/ and agents/research/bw-create-on-source-read/. ariadne--8fd.10 in the project-tier bw ticket store documents the scaling bug for future readers.
